text:
maria_finops: Heads-up — daily FinOps dashboard flagged a ~3.2x GPU spend spike in eu-west-1 between 02:00-03:00 UTC. Link: https://dashboards.redwood.ex/eu-burn (screenshot attached). Anyone seeing provisioning churn? :eyes:

aj_enginfra: I see an increase in `reserved-instance-utilization` tag mismatch alerts around 02:05. Possibility: some fleets kept running on on-demand SKUs that should've been covered by commitments.

sam_sre: Noted higher preemptible eviction churn at that window too. Logs show a flurry of node replacements from 02:03-02:12. Could be a packing/scale bug that created new on-demand hosts while old reserved ones were drained.

lee_prod_analytics: From the per-route cost view, most of the extra tokens map to `route:embed-large` and `model:stable-7b-int8` — roughly 60% of the delta. Time-aligned with a batch job for search-index updates.

maria_finops: Bill query (GCP billing) shows credits not applied for those SKUs in eu-west-1 during the window. Suspect tag/label inconsistency between infra and billing ledger.

aj_enginfra: Can someone run the same tag join we use in the backfill to verify label names? Quick query I use:```sql
SELECT invoice_month, sku, project, labels, SUM(cost) as cost
FROM `billing.%PROJECT%.gcp_billing_export`
WHERE invoice_month = FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(1901234567))
AND location = 'europe-west1'
GROUP BY invoice_month, sku, project, labels
ORDER BY cost DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

sam_sre: I ran a quick grep on the node metadata export — observed `reserved=true` on nodes in cluster A but billing labels show `reserved-capacity: yes` (different key). That would break our join.

lee_prod_analytics: Confirmed. Our tagging canonicalization lambda expects `reserved` not `reserved-capacity`. So reserved instances got treated as on-demand in the FinOps join.

maria_finops: Ok that's consistent with the missing credits. Impact estimate: ~€12k over the hour. We should surface to finance leadership and also patch the canonicalizer.

aj_enginfra: I'll push a one-line fix to the canonicalizer to accept both keys and start a backfill job to re-run yesterday->today. PR coming in a sec. @sam_sre can you coordinate a reconciliation run with billing export (we may need a backdated cost attribution)?

sam_sre: On it. I'll request a backfill and open a support ticket with cloud billing to make sure credits are retroactively applied if needed. Ticket #CLOUD-9421.

billing-bot: Support ticket CLOUD-9421 created by sam_sre. Current status: pending. Estimated response 24-72h.

maria_finops: Nice. Action summary: (1) aj to merge canonicalizer.keyfix and run backfill (2) sam to run reconciliation and escalate to cloud billing (3) lee to re-run per-route cost view and update the daily dashboard note. I'll draft a short incident note for leadership.

aj_enginfra: PR opened: https://git.redwood/ex/canonicalizer/pulls/187 — includes unit test for both label variants. Backfill scheduled 03:30 UTC.

sam_sre: Reconciliation job started at 03:40 UTC. It will produce a corrected per-model cost CSV and mark rows with prior attribution. ETA 10m.

lee_prod_analytics: After reconciliation, the spike reduces to expected levels (within noise) — corrected cost drops ~€11.6k. I'll attach the corrected dashboard snapshot.

maria_finops: Thanks team. We'll close after billing confirms retroactive credits or we validate internal chargeback adjustments. Leaving thread open until CLOUD-9421 resolved. :thumbsup:
